subject.title: fix(settings): deep-merge nested settings objects across scopes (#102318)

question: Should OpenClaw accept recursive plain-object merging across settings scopes here, and should this PR or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102330 be the landing path for the linked settings bug?
rationale: The code change fixes the source-reproducible bug, but it also changes upgrade behavior for nested settings and there are two viable open candidate PRs with different implementation/test tradeoffs.

options.title: Land one combined recursive fix
options.body: Accept recursive nested settings semantics and land one candidate, porting the best helper and regression coverage together before closing the duplicate.

options.title: Narrow to retry.provider
options.body: Limit the compatibility footprint by merging only the observed `retry.provider` nested fields until maintainers define broader settings semantics.

options.title: Pause for settings policy
options.body: Hold both candidate PRs until maintainers decide whether nested settings objects should always merge recursively or may replace wholesale.

recommendation.title: Land one combined recursive fix
recommendation.body: Accept recursive nested settings semantics and land one candidate, porting the best helper and regression coverage together before closing the duplicate.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent merge history connect this person most directly to the settings merge and provider retry surfaces.
